states.name: quattro
states.gap: Syntax marks are 36 grey levels darker than A's — every '#', '##', '*' and '**' is gray 122 (#7A7A7A, ~4.4:1 on the 249 paper) where A sets them at gray 158 (#9E9E9E, ~2.6:1) — so '**bottle**' reads as four hard dots flanking a word rather than a word.
states.gapTheirs: Markers sit inside the text column instead of hanging, so the passage has four different left edges: body at x=622, H1 text at 667 (+23 css px), list text at 668 (+23 css px), H2 text at 691 (+35 css px). B holds every text edge within 6 device px (3 css px) of one spine and hangs '#' 26 css, '##' 38 css, '-' 23 css into the margin.
states.verdict: A's markers are the column and the words are the indent — your eye lands on a different x for the heading, the body and the list, and you feel the wobble on every block change. B does the only thing that matters here: hangs the '#', '##' and '-' out into the margin so all fourteen lines of prose, both headings and all three list items return to one edge. A does buy a quieter marker grey (158 vs 122), and it wastes it by setting its own list dashes at 122 — two syntax greys in one document, which is worse than B's one loud one. B also runs a 37 css pitch to A's 38 at identical 15 css cap height, so A's paragraphs are the airier and more diffuse of the two.
secondary: Type size effectively identical: cap height 30 dev / x-height 24 dev in both; advance 23.15 dev (A) vs 23.45 dev (B), a ~1.3% tracking difference, not a size step
Both lead loose for prose — A ~2.00x, B ~1.95x — neither is at an iA-Writer-ish 1.6-1.7
Caret is a wash: 3 css px wide, full line-box tall, #00B5FF in both
Both space headings symmetrically at exactly 2 pitches before and after, so a heading does not read as belonging to the text below it
Body ink 28 and paper 249 identical in both (Dark & light's territory, not this piece's)
Same typeface, true italic (single-storey italic 'a', not obliqued), and H1/H2 set at body size in bold rather than scaled up — identical in both
B's hanging indent lands ~5-7 dev (2.5-3.5 css px) left of the body spine on headings and list items rather than dead flush
B's hanging markers push the inked block ~22 css px left of the viewport centre; A's block is centred
Measure: A ~71 chars / 817 css px, B ~69 chars / 812 css px — both in range

states.name: mono
states.gap: Weaker heading authority: B's H1 has the same 24px x-height as its body text and leans entirely on a 7px stem (0.29 of x-height) with the '#' greyed out, so the heading row's leftmost mark is the faintest ink on the page; A's heading carries an 8px stem (0.35 of x-height) and reads harder on a fast scroll. B is also set ~1.6% larger in the same column (x-height 24px vs 23px, advance ~26.1px vs ~25.7px), so line 2 wraps 4 characters earlier (60 vs 64) and the paragraph runs longer.
states.gapTheirs: No ink hierarchy for markdown marks: the '#' and both '*' fences peak at exactly #FFFFFF — pixel-identical to the heading and italic they mark (measured max=255 in both marker and text regions) — and the '#' is set at the heading's full bold stem (8px vs body's 6px). B drops both marks to #7A7A7A at regular weight against #1C1C1C text, roughly a 3.5x lightness step; A gives zero.
states.verdict: A prints the scaffolding at the same volume as the prose: '# The Lighthouse' reads as a five-character bold sentence starting with a hash, and '*Nothing out there is ever in a hurry,*' is fenced in two full-brightness white asterisks that punch a hole in the middle of a line you are trying to read for rhythm. B greys those same marks to #7A7A7A and un-bolds them, so the eye lands on 'The Lighthouse' and on the italic clause, not on the punctuation that produced them. Everything else is a wash — pitch 73.5px vs 74.7px, x-height 23px vs 24px, paragraph gap 1.99x vs 1.98x pitch, identical typeface — which means the marker treatment is the whole decision. A writer would feel it within one paragraph of typing emphasis.
secondary: Neither steps the H1 in size: heading x-height equals body x-height in both (A 23/23, B 24/24) — an H1 distinguished by weight alone
Line pitch effectively identical: A ~73.5px, B ~74.7px; leading ratio ~1.71 vs ~1.70
Blank-line spacing correct in both: heading baseline to first body baseline is 146px (A) / 148px (B) = 1.99 / 1.98 line pitches

A's white-on-dark ink blooms: body stems 6px at a 23px x-height (0.26) vs B's 5px at 24px (0.21) — A's ink runs ~24% fatter per unit size, and A's bold heading 'h' fills in (stem and shoulder merge into a 21px blob where B keeps 10px and 9px strokes with a visible counter)
Both still spend a full monospace advance (~26px) on each inline '*', so even B's italic clause is visibly fenced rather than flush
No caret visible in either crop, so caret weight could not be compared
